title: When the Bakery Sings
premise: Jonah Brightwater, once the most celebrated wedding planner in the city, walked away after a catastrophic failure of love and duty left him convinced that promises are just beautifully wrapped lies. Five years later, running a modest bakery-adjacent event studio, he is forced to co-plan one final high-profile wedding with Wren Calloway, his brilliant rival and the person he loved and abandoned a decade ago. A snowstorm strands them together with their shared past, and as the wedding unravels around them, Jonah must finally speak the sentence he has rehearsed for ten years—before Wren signs a contract that will take her across the ocean for good. The story ends with Jonah choosing visibility over safety, confessing at the altar of someone else's wedding, and Wren choosing him over the escape she thought she wanted.
about_author: Dominic Underhill is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, chapels, and snowed-in small towns. He lives above a bakery he refuses to name, where he claims the bread tells him all his plot twists.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet him measuring out a stranger's anniversary party with obsessive precision, revealing through flashbacks the disaster five years ago that ended his career and his belief in weddings. Emotional beat: controlled grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Rival's Card
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Calloway, now a rising star planner, receives the Meridian wedding contract—and discovers the venue has already hired a local consultant: Jonah. She remembers everything he never said. Emotional beat: old anger sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The first meeting in ten years is all professional armor and barbed politeness. They agree to split duties down an invisible line drawn through the venue. Emotional beat: two people pretending a decade didn't happen.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah catalogs his carefully rebuilt life—the routine, the rented room, the rule against second chances—while scouting the venue alone and finding Wren's handwriting in an old planning notebook from their twenties. Emotional beat: nostalgia as threat.

chapters.title: Cake Tasting for Two
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced together by a caterer cancellation, they taste cakes while trading passive-aggressive compliments. A shared laugh escapes before either can stop it. Emotional beat: the first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: The Bride Who Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The bride, Delia, reveals she chose both planners deliberately—she was a guest at the legendary wedding that broke them both, and she wants whatever magic they made back then. Emotional beat: being seen without permission.

chapters.title: What the Storm Brought
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. An early blizzard seals the mountain venue with the couple, staff, and both planners inside. Generators fail; the rehearsal collapses into improvisation by candlelight. Emotional beat: chaos stripping away pretense.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Trapped in the wine cellar inventory room, Wren finally names what happened a decade ago—Jonah's family duty, the arranged path he chose over her, the sentence he never finished saying. Emotional beat: accusation met with silence.

chapters.title: Bread at Midnight
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Unable to sleep, Jonah bakes in the venue kitchen, and Wren appears, drawn by the smell. They work dough side by side without speaking, hands almost touching. Emotional beat: intimacy returning through muscle memory.

chapters.title: Delia's Doubt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm strains the bride and groom; Delia wobbles, asking Jonah privately whether love is worth the risk. His answer surprises himself. Emotional beat: counseling another toward what he fled.

chapters.title: The Contract on the Table
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Phone signal returns briefly: Wren learns her dream firm in Lisbon wants her permanently—if she signs within the week. She says nothing to Jonah. Emotional beat: hope curdling into countdown.

chapters.title: Snowbound Confessions
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. By firelight, Jonah tells Wren the full truth of five years ago—the bankruptcy, the shame, why he vanished from everyone, not just her. She softens but won't unclench. Emotional beat: honesty offered, not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A near-kiss interrupted by the groom's emergency; they spend the night fixing a collapsed floral arch, laughing like they used to. Wren pulls back first. Emotional beat: desire outrunning fear, then fear winning.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah realizes staying invisible was always the real cowardice—not just with Wren, but with his own ambition. He begins quietly redesigning the wedding as something braver than the couple asked for. Emotional beat: the turn inward becomes the turn outward.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Linen Closet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the unsent letter Jonah wrote her ten years ago, tucked in old linens from their first venue. She reads it twice and cries in a supply closet. Emotional beat: the past demanding a verdict.

chapters.title: Rivalry Refused
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The roads clear; the couple's families arrive with demands that threaten to split the planners' unified vision again. This time Jonah and Wren defend each other publicly. Emotional beat: alliance becoming something undeniable.

chapters.title: Lisbon or Here
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah discovers the Lisbon offer and confronts Wren, who accuses him of reading her mail and of wanting her only when leaving is possible. Harsh words, real wounds. Emotional beat: love weaponized into distance.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Eve of the wedding. Wren packs, signs nothing, and walks the empty venue, remembering every version of Jonah she has known. Jonah stands outside her door and doesn't knock. Emotional beat: the darkest hour before speech.

chapters.title: A Wedding Falls Apart
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The ceremony day brings catastrophe: the officiant is stranded, the flowers freeze, and Delia's cold feet return. Everything Jonah planned fails at once. Emotional beat: control finally, fully lost.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Improvising the ceremony, Jonah hands the mic to no one—he simply says it, the sentence rehearsed for a decade, in front of everyone: that he chose duty over love once and will spend every remaining day choosing otherwise. Emotional beat: climax; vulnerability as public act.

chapters.title: What Wren Chose
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tears up the Lisbon contract in front of the guests—or rather, asks Delia to keep it as confetti—and answers him with a kiss as the improvised vows continue around them. Emotional beat: release and joy.

chapters.title: When the Bakery Sings
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating. Months later, Jonah and Wren run a joint studio above his bakery; the ovens warm the planning office, and every wedding they build starts with bread and ends with truth. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed—love as the thing worth passing on.
